newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq complains to UN over Turkish border raids.
newsitem.headline: Iraq complains to UN over Turkish border raids.

text.p: Baghdad has called on the United Nations to investigate alleged Turkish bombings and incursions into northern Iraq, official newspapers reported on Friday.
They quoted a letter sent by Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali and head of the Security Council as saying:
"Iraq urges the U.N...to conduct immediate and comprehensive investigation of the continuous Turkish bombing of Iraqi towns and villages and entering illegally to its territory.

"The Turkish ground troops supported by jet fighters and helicopter gunship penetrated on November 3, 1996 two km (1.2 mile) deep inside Iraqi territory...and a team of six Turks entered Dohuk's villages and towns and distributed questionnaires among people in order to collect personal information."
Turkey often strikes across the border at separatist rebels of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) who uses bases in northern Iraq in their fight for self-rule in southeast Turkey.
In Ankara, a foreign ministry spokesman said Turkey would reply to the Iraqi protest.

"Turkey respects Iraq's territorial integrity and independence but terrorist elements are taking advantage of a power vacuum in northern Iraq to cross the border and harm the Turkish people," spokesman Sermet Atacanli told Reuters.
"Turkey, using the right of self defence given to it by international law, carries out these operations from time to time," he said.

Northern Iraq has been held by Iraqi Kurdish groups since the end of the 1991 Gulf War. The Iraqi Kurds have been unable or unwilling to stamp out the PKK presence on their territory. "Iraq is not in control of the north of Iraq," Atacanli said.
More than 21,000 people have died in Turkey's 12-year-old Kurdish rebel conflict. A six-week drive into Iraq last year involving 30,000 Turkish troops failed to dislodge the PKK.
"Such Turkish troops practices jeopardise stability in the region which suffers from an extraordinary situation created by the U.S. and its allies in northern Iraq," the Iraqi letter said.
U.S., British and French warplanes police a no-fly zone in northern Iraq to shield Iraqi Kurds from possible military attacks by Baghdad's troops.
